headline: New Jersey's Drone Ranger Reunites Lost Pets With Families
meta_description: A 64-year-old New Jersey resident uses thermal imaging drones to locate missing animals, reuniting over 120 pets with their families.
summary_short: One man's fleet of 18 drones is changing how lost animals get found. The 64-year-old 'Drone Ranger' has already brought joy back to more than 120 families.
body:
A 64-year-old New Jersey resident has turned drone technology into a lifeline for pet owners, using a fleet of 18 drones—including thermal imaging models—to locate and reunite lost animals with their families. The self-proclaimed "Drone Ranger" has successfully brought home more than 120 pets through this innovative approach.

The thermal imaging capability gives the operation a crucial edge in searches that might otherwise end in heartbreak. By detecting body heat signatures from above, the drones can spot missing animals in dense brush, wooded areas, or at night when ground searches become impossible.

What makes this effort remarkable is not just the technology itself, but the person wielding it: a retired individual who has channeled experience and resourcefulness into solving a deeply human problem. Every reunited pet represents a family's relief and a life recovered.
quick_facts: 64-year-old New Jersey resident operates lost-pet search service
Fleet of 18 drones includes thermal imaging models
Over 120 pets successfully reunited with families
